claim: Live cleanup controls accept a Cause whose Die is not the permission failure of remove. They require some Die, the first Fail equal to the injected PermissionDenied, Cause.pretty containing PermissionDenied, and the directory still present. SystemError.message is `${_tag}: ${module}.${method}...` and causePrettyErrors prints every Fail, so the substring is satisfied by the injected Fail even when the Die is a different defect.
evidence: After snapshot. lint-security.test.ts:109-112 (inject witness+chmod 000 and return the Fail at 76-82). purge-security.test.ts:163-165 and exists loop 167-171 (inject at 135-143). step-git-exec.test.ts:414-417 and 575-578 (inject at 389-395 and 550-556); findErrorOption at 409 and 570 identifies only the Fail. Installed Effect: PlatformError.ts:128-131 SystemError.message; effect.ts:433-434 causePretty; effect.ts:284-295 causePrettyErrors prints Fail error and Die defect; effect.ts:352-354 causePrettyMessage uses error.message; effect.ts:157-164 findError returns the first Fail; effect.ts:171 hasDies is reasons.some(isDieReason). Counterexample that passes all four checks: scoped remove dies with new Error("boom") while the directory remains. skills-command.test.ts:335-338 is the strict pattern in the same batch: tapped remove error, method remove, pathOrDescriptor === root, assertExitFailure against Cause.die of that error.
proposedFix: Assert the Die separately from the Fail: defect is a SystemError, method is remove, path is the denied root, and the cause is exactly that one Fail plus that one Die. Do not use Cause.pretty().toContain("PermissionDenied"). Match skills-command.test.ts:335-338.

claim: Setup and acquisition-failure controls that only check Cause.findErrorOption plus exists===false accept a later Die when removal still succeeds. Body controls that use Cause.squash accept a later Die when the first Die defect is the injected object, and they accept an earlier Fail whose error is that same object. Interrupt controls use Cause.hasInterruptsOnly and reject an extra Die.
evidence: After snapshot assertion arms: lint-security.test.ts:99-104; purge-security.test.ts:156-159; step-git-exec.test.ts:404-409 and 565-570; regenerate-merge-driver.test.ts:122-127. Installed Effect effect.ts:157-168 findError/findErrorOption return the first Fail only; effect.ts:261-269 causeSquash returns the first Fail immediately else the first Die defect; effect.ts:218-219 hasInterruptsOnly requires every reason to be Interrupt. The tests do not install a second dying finalizer; this is a control gap, not a second finalizer present in the batch.
proposedFix: Compare the observed cause to exactly one expected Fail or exactly one expected Die via assertExitFailure, as skills-command.test.ts does. Keep hasInterruptsOnly for interruption.

claim: regenerate-merge-driver implements a cleanup-failure injection and assertions that its mode loop never selects. step-git-exec implements body-failure squash arms that its two mode loops never select. Deleting those arms changes no passing test. The regenerate gap is unreachable coverage, not a passing false-green.
evidence: After snapshot regenerate-merge-driver.test.ts:59 loops ["setup failure","body failure","interruption"]. Cleanup injection at 99-103 and assertions at 132-135 are unreachable. A's source report does not claim a merge-driver cleanup case. step-git-exec.test.ts:348 and :513 loop ["setup failure","interruption","cleanup failure"]. Body-failure arms at 406-407 and 567-568 never run. If cleanup failure were added to the regenerate loop without a Die-identity assertion, it would inherit cleanup-pretty-matches-injected-fail.
proposedFix: Either add the missing mode to the loop (regenerate cleanup must use the Die-identity assertion from cleanup-pretty-matches-injected-fail) or delete the dead arms.
